content_brand_lead: Linking to SOTF Mods from your mod page, video or server? Use these files and keep the rules below.
content_brand_legal_text: The SOTF Mods name and logo identify this community site. You may use them to refer to or link to the site; any other use needs our permission.
content_brand_link_text: Copy this snippet into your README, website or mod description. It points to the live logo, so it always stays up to date.
content_brand_logos_text: Each asset comes in a Night version for dark backgrounds and a Day version for light ones. Prefer SVG; use PNG where SVG is not accepted.
content_dev_endpoints_text: Anonymous, cacheable and CORS-enabled. The reference documents parameters, responses and errors for each one.
content_dev_errors_text: The code field of an error is one of these. Each problem’s type URI points to its row here.
content_dev_legacy_deprecated_text: These routes keep answering until {date}, then they will be retired. Their responses carry these headers:
content_dev_legacy_deviations: Intentional differences from the old behaviour
content_dev_legacy_retired_text: Every method on these routes answers 410 Gone with this body:
content_dev_legacy_text: The API of the first version of the site still answers on api.sotf-mods.com/api/* and sotf-mods.com/api/*, so RedManager, UpdatesChecker and in-game mods keep working. New integrations should use v2.
content_dev_limits_text: Above a limit the API answers 429 with a Retry-After header. Cache responses and honour ETags; you will rarely come close.
content_dev_link_docs_text: Every v2 endpoint with schemas and examples, interactive.
content_dev_link_legacy_text: Still served; frozen routes sunset on {date}.
content_dev_link_openapi_text: The machine-readable spec, to generate a client.
content_draft_text: This text describes how SOTF Mods works today, but it has not been reviewed by a lawyer yet. It may change before it is final; we will date every change.

content_install_help_text: Check whether the current game patch broke your mods, or ask the community. Include your game version, RedLoader version and the mods you use.
content_install_kit_text: A staff-picked set of mods that work well together. A good first load-out.
content_kelvin_credit: KelvinSeek is made and maintained by {author}; SOTF Mods only runs the API it talks to. Kelvin and Sons of the Forest belong to Endnight Games; this is a fan project.
content_kelvin_description: KelvinSeek lets you chat with Kelvin in Sons of the Forest and give him orders in plain words. How it works, its limits and what happens to your messages.
content_kelvin_dev_hint: Building something similar? The endpoint is part of the legacy API:
content_kelvin_history_text: It was previously known as Kelvin-GPT. The old version that asked for your own OpenAI key is retired: that route exposed the key in the address and now answers “Gone”.
content_kelvin_how_1: Install RedLoader and the KelvinSeek mod.
content_kelvin_how_2: In game, walk up to Kelvin and press E to open the notepad.
content_kelvin_how_3: Press T to type, write your message and press Enter.
content_kelvin_how_4: Or use the console: “askkelvin …” sends a message, “clearkelvinchathistory” starts a fresh conversation.
content_kelvin_install_hint: New to mods? Start with the guide:
content_kelvin_lead: Write to Kelvin in plain words and he answers — and does what you ask, from fetching logs to building a shelter.
content_kelvin_limits_budget: The AI service has a daily budget. When it runs out, Kelvin still understands you: he picks the closest known order without AI until the next day.
content_kelvin_limits_busy: If you write too fast, Kelvin asks for a break for a few seconds. Nothing is lost.

match: Up to {perMinute__number} messages a minute and {perDay__number} a day per player.

content_kelvin_privacy_ai: The text of your messages is sent to the AI provider to generate the answer. Don’t write personal information.
